Exploring lower-reduction actuation

My work on cycloidal joints led me to study a lower-reduction planetary layout for quasi-direct-drive actuation.

I’m working out how to fit the sun, planets, ring, bearings, and output structure into a compact motor package. The CAD history retains several gear candidates as I revise the geometry and interfaces.

Checking the gear geometry

For a simple planetary set, both gear meshes must agree on the carrier spacing. This links the tooth counts to the sun–planet and planet–ring center distances.

Compatible tooth counts
Nr = Ns + 2Np

For gears sharing the same module and standard pitch geometry, the ring tooth count Nr equals the sun tooth count Ns plus twice the planet tooth count Np.

Fixed ring · Sun input · Carrier output
G = 1 + Nr / Ns
PCDcarrier = m(Ns + Np)

G is the ideal speed-reduction ratio for this configuration. The carrier pitch-circle diameter follows from the module m and the sun–planet center distance.

Packaging and assembly questions

  • Compare reduction candidates against the available motor and housing envelope.
  • Check planet placement and support, output interfaces, and assembly access.
  • Fit the encoder and motor controller into the mechanical layout.
  • Resolve the assembly geometry before committing to manufacturing.

Current stage

PROJECT STATUS

CAD and packaging in development.

I’m still comparing gear candidates and working through the actuator assembly. Next, I need to specify the materials and manufacturing approach, then build and test a prototype. The final ratio and physical performance, including continuous torque, strength, and fatigue life, remain unverified.
